claims.text: The representative nanoscale PGM catalyst has outstanding ethanol-oxidation activity.
The representative nanoscale PGM catalyst has outstanding ethanol-oxidation selectivity.
The representative nanoscale PGM catalyst has outstanding durability during ethanol oxidation.
Its ethanol-oxidation performance is governed by synergistic modulation of the d-band electronic structure at adjacent, compositionally heterogeneous active sites.
Local electronic diversity optimizes the binding and transformation of ethanol and its oxidation intermediates.
The proposed electronic-site diversity promotes the complete 12-electron oxidation pathway.
The original catalyst is a nanoscale PGM-based material, potentially a high-entropy or multi-principal-element alloy.
The original catalyst has a homogeneous distribution of alloy constituents.
Its alloy constituents create heterogeneous active sites at the surface.
A chosen non-PGM alloying component is responsible for generating local electronic heterogeneity and shifting the d-band center.
Reducing that component will reduce compositional heterogeneity and produce a more uniform or shifted d-band profile.
Adjacent electronically distinct atoms tune the d-band center so that adsorption energies of ethanol and its intermediates are balanced.
The proposed adsorption balance is strong enough to activate ethanol but weak enough to permit desorption before poisoning.
This adsorption balance facilitates complete ethanol oxidation.
Avoidance of poisoning through the proposed adsorption balance improves long-term durability.
Reducing compositional heterogeneity will decrease EOR current density relative to the original catalyst.
Reducing compositional heterogeneity will shift the product distribution toward partial-oxidation products.
The proposed mechanism applies under kinetically controlled EOR conditions involving the complete 12-electron and 12-proton process.
The proposed relationship may fail when mass transport or other non-kinetic factors dominate.
Analogous studies support d-band tuning through active-site heterogeneity.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having a homogeneous distribution of alloy constituents, while the proposed mediator and intervention depend on compositional heterogeneity. Atomic-scale chemical diversity could reconcile these descriptions, but the hypothesis does not explain that distinction.
